# Theme: llm-psychology

Jagged intelligence, ghosts vs animals, sycophancy, how to model LLMs.

29 ideas, newest first.

- 2026-10-02 · [Test a model by asking if coordinates are land or water](../ideas/2026-10-02-land-or-water-eval.md) — Ask a model many times whether a latitude and longitude is land or water and plot the answers, and it draws the world from text alone. *(Anthropic period)*
- 2026-08-02 · [Models cannot yet check their own work in video and games](../ideas/2026-08-02-models-cannot-audit-video-and-games.md) — Worlds and games expose a gap: models cannot watch video or play a game natively, so they audit their output slowly through screenshots. *(Anthropic period)*
- 2026-07-21 · [Model self-knowledge comes from text about models](../ideas/2026-07-21-model-self-awareness-from-pretraining.md) — Models learn about themselves from pretraining text in which people discuss them, so their self-awareness lags and is incomplete, but it grows.

- 2026-04-09 · [People judge AI differently because they use different AI](../ideas/2026-04-09-ai-capability-gap-two-groups.md) — Free-tier users and professionals on frontier models see different AI, and both are partly right; gains peak in verifiable, valuable domains.
- 2026-03-31 · [You can outsource thinking, but not understanding](../ideas/2026-03-31-understanding-is-the-bottleneck.md) — Agents can do the work, but your own understanding sets the limit on directing them; use LLMs to build understanding, and keep reading.

- 2026-03-25 · [Closing follow-up questions in chatbots are engagement bait](../ideas/2026-03-25-follow-up-questions-engagementmaxxing.md) — The habit of ending every answer with a question probably wins A/B tests, but it feels unnatural and manipulative to him.
- 2026-03-25 · [LLM memory over-uses old facts about you](../ideas/2026-03-25-memory-personalization-overreach.md) — Memory features treat one old question as a lasting interest; models over-use given context, and naive retrieval cannot tell what is fleeting.

- 2026-03-21 · [AI personality should feel like a teammate, and it takes deliberate work](../ideas/2026-03-21-ai-personality-like-rocky.md) — Assistants feel too safe and corporate; a teammate-like personality needs long persona files and an owner who cares, not new technology.
- 2026-03-20 · [Jagged intelligence follows verifiability and training focus](../ideas/2026-03-20-jagged-intelligence-follows-verifiability.md) — Models are sharp where rewards are checkable and where labs put training effort, and dull elsewhere; check that your task is on the model's rails.
- 2026-02-12 · [A pretrained LLM can simulate a population, not one persona](../ideas/2026-02-12-simulate-a-population-not-one-persona.md) — A base model is trained on many kinds of people, so it can simulate a population; the open problems are entropy, fidelity and use.
- 2026-01-26 · [Coding agents make subtle conceptual mistakes, so watch them](../ideas/2026-01-26-coding-agents-make-subtle-conceptual-mistakes.md) — Agent errors are no longer syntax slips but wrong assumptions and bloat, so keep an IDE open and review code you care about.
- 2025-12-10 · [LLM judges grade too freely and recognise who wrote the text](../ideas/2025-12-10-llm-grader-identity-bias.md) — Grading old HN threads, the model gave grades too easily and was biased by author names, and prompt tuning helped only a little.
- 2025-12-07 · [Ask the LLM to simulate experts, not to give its opinion](../ideas/2025-12-07-llms-simulate-there-is-no-you.md) — There is no 'you' inside the model, so ask it to simulate a panel of suitable people instead of asking for its own opinion.
- 2025-11-29 · [LLMs are shaped by commercial evolution, not biological evolution](../ideas/2025-11-29-llms-shaped-by-commercial-evolution.md) — Animal minds come from survival pressure, while LLMs come from imitating text, task rewards and user votes, which explains sycophancy and spiky skills.
- 2025-11-18 · [Public benchmarks are gameable, so keep your own evals](../ideas/2025-11-18-go-talk-to-the-model-private-evals.md) — Benchmarks are verifiable, so labs train toward them and scores mislead; talk to each model and test it on a private set of your own tasks.
- 2025-10-17 · [Model outputs are silently collapsed, so synthetic data needs entropy](../ideas/2025-10-17-synthetic-data-and-model-collapse.md) — Each sample from a model looks fine but the set is narrow; training on your own output makes models worse, so seek outside variety.
- 2025-10-17 · [Weights are a hazy memory; the context window is working memory](../ideas/2025-10-17-weights-hazy-memory-context-working-memory.md) — A model recalls training data vaguely but reads its context directly, so paste the source text instead of asking it to remember.
- 2025-10-01 · [LLMs are ghosts, not animals](../ideas/2025-10-01-llms-are-ghosts-not-animals.md) — Frontier LLMs are statistical distillations of human text, a different kind of mind from animals; pretraining is a stand-in for evolution, not a copy of it.
- 2025-08-09 · [Models are too agentic by default, so state stakes and scope](../ideas/2025-08-09-models-too-agentic-state-stakes-and-scope.md) — Tuned models over-think simple questions and search the whole repo, so tell them the scope and the depth you want.
- 2025-06-17 · [LLMs are people spirits with superpowers and deficits](../ideas/2025-06-17-llms-are-people-spirits-with-deficits.md) — An LLM simulates people, so it recalls like a savant, is jagged, forgets everything between sessions and can be tricked; work around all four.
- 2025-02-27 · [Check which tools the model has before you trust its answer](../ideas/2025-02-27-check-which-tools-the-model-has.md) — Search and a code interpreter fix recent facts and hard arithmetic; models without them guess, so ask for the tool.
- 2025-02-27 · [Try a fast model first, switch to a thinking model for hard problems](../ideas/2025-02-27-fast-model-first-thinking-model-for-hard.md) — Know which model and tier you use; start fast, move to a reasoning model for hard code and math, and compare several vendors.
- 2025-02-27 · [Treat LLM output as a first draft and check the sources](../ideas/2025-02-27-llm-output-is-a-first-draft.md) — Even with search or deep research, answers can be wrong; use citations, primary sources and a read of the generated code.
- 2024-11-29 · [Asking an AI is like asking the average data labeler](../ideas/2024-11-29-asking-an-ai-is-asking-the-average-data-labeler.md) — A model's answer reflects a skilled, average data labeler distilled into weights, and RL changes this only where answers can be verified.
- 2023-12-08 · [Hallucination is the LLM's main feature, so the system must check it](../ideas/2023-12-08-hallucination-is-the-llms-feature.md) — An LLM is a dream machine steered by prompts, so the system around it must check its output with search, tools and verification.
